docs.task: How the native loop decides when to compact a conversation and what constants it uses.

asks: How does the native loop decide when to compact a conversation?

data_flow.step: Before the loop, the window is resolved from the models.dev catalog by the route's model id, falling back to DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW (200,000). The max output is resolved the same way with fallback DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT (32,000). `measured` and `measured_len` start at 0 and `failed_compaction_at` at None.
At the top of each turn (max MAX_TURNS = 400), next = measured + estimate_tokens(messages not covered by the last response).
Compaction runs if next >= 0.95 * window, the retry guard passes (no earlier failure, or next >= failed_at + 0.02 * window), and the last message is a user turn.

Run::compact emits a Status delta ('Compacting the conversation: about {tokens} of {window} context tokens used.'), calls provider.compact(req, COMPACT_INSTRUCTIONS, cancel), adds the summarization usage via add_usage with no call ids, and emits a result Status.

On a summary, the loop appends the AFTER_COMPACTION user turn, stores the new window as a `compaction` transcript record via host.record_message, and replaces `messages`. stored_messages later rebuilds from the last compaction record on resume.

The request is sent in the same iteration, without a second threshold check. The response's usage is turned into context_tokens with context_of, and (measured, measured_len) is set to that value and the new message count, so the next iteration measures from the post-compaction size.

patterns.description: On every iteration of the turn loop (up to MAX_TURNS), before the request is sent, the loop computes `next`, the estimated size of the next request, and compares it with COMPACT_AT times the window. Three conditions must all hold: next >= 0.95 * window; the retry guard allows it; the last message is a user turn (tool results are sent as a user message, so this is true after tool results, and false right after an assistant message with no tool results). `measured` and `measured_len` are updated after every response (`(measured, measured_len) = (usage.context_tokens, messages.len())`), so `next` is the last response's context plus an estimate for only the messages added since. Outcomes: Ok(Some) replaces messages, appends the AFTER_COMPACTION user turn, records a `compaction` transcript record, and clears failed_compaction_at; Ok(None) or a non-cancel Err sets failed_compaction_at = Some(next) (the Err case also emits a Status delta); Err(Cancelled) returns a Cancelled result.
patterns.name: Compaction check before each request

patterns.description: The loop does not count tokens. context_of sums the response's input, cache read, cache write, and output tokens (the size the next request starts from) and stores it in usage.context_tokens. Messages not yet covered by a response (tool results and any appended user turns) are estimated at 4 characters per token over text, thinking, tool input JSON, tool result content, redacted thinking data, opaque JSON, and compaction summary plus value.
patterns.name: Size estimate without a tokenizer

document.problem: The native agent loop (crates/ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs, Run::execute) replaces the conversation with a summary when the next request would nearly fill the model's context window. The decision depends on a size estimate, a window lookup, a 95% threshold, a retry guard after a failed compaction, and a structural condition on the last message.

submit.findings_summary: Before each request, Run::execute computes next = last response's context (input + cache read + cache write + output tokens) plus a 4-chars-per-token estimate of newer messages. It compacts when next >= COMPACT_AT (0.95) x window, the last message is a user turn, and the retry guard passes (after a failed or empty compaction, next must grow by COMPACT_RETRY_GROWTH = 0.02 x window). The window comes from the models.dev catalog (pricing::context_window) with DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 200_000 as fallback; the output limit falls back to DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT = 32_000. Other constants: MAX_TURNS 400, MAX_TOKEN_CONTINUES 3, EMIT_LIMIT 8 KiB, CLEANUP_GRACE 3 s, plus COMPACT_INSTRUCTIONS and AFTER_COMPACTION texts. On success the summary replaces all messages and is stored as a `compaction` transcript record; docs/internals/executors.md (Long runs) and two tests in tests.rs encode the 95% and 200k numbers.

docs.task: How the global config is defined, loaded, validated, and passed to the native executor.

asks: How the global config is defined
How it is passed to the native executor

data_flow.step: Startup: `ensure_global_config` writes `GlobalConfig::default()` with `save_toml` (atomic temp file plus rename) when the file does not exist.

Startup: `build` loads the file with `load_toml` (missing file gives Default; a parse error aborts startup with context), then runs `ostra_sandbox::validate::global(&global.sandbox)` and aborts on the first issue. The copy feeds `Providers::from_config`, `EnvStatus::detect`, `access`, and `Shared.global_cache`.
The one `NativeExecutor` is constructed once with `Arc<Providers>`, a skill resolver, and optional connectors; it stores no GlobalConfig and no config values.
Per execution, the engine calls `Services::global()`, which `ServerServices` forwards to `Shared::global()` (re-read, last-good fallback).

The runner resolves the route with `resolve_route(&global, &settings, RouteQuery{..})`. A `RouteError` becomes a denied execution recorded as `route: ...`, never a fallback. Tier names resolve through `global.tiers[executor.tier_table()]`.

The runner builds `ExecContext` (merged permissions, `enforce_tool_calls`, `sandbox_readable`, workspace sandbox choices) and `ExecutionSpec` (route, effort, prompt, capabilities, timeout, ctx), then calls `executor.run(spec, host, token)`.

`NativeExecutor::run` wraps the spec in `Run` and calls `Run::execute`. `execute` resolves the provider from `spec.route.model`, computes `window` from `ostra_core::pricing::context_window` (default 200,000), and compares the next request's estimated size against the constant `COMPACT_AT * window`.

Inside `execute`, `mcp_secret_vars(ctx)` and `sandbox_for(ctx, host)` each call `load_toml` on `global_config_path()` again to get credential variable names and the `[sandbox]` table, merged with the workspace's choices from `ctx.sandbox()`.

document.problem: The global config (`config.toml`) is a serde struct in ostra-core. The server re-reads it per call with a last-good fallback, and the engine reads it per execution to resolve routes and merge permissions. The NativeExecutor is not handed a GlobalConfig: it receives an ExecutionSpec (route, ExecContext) and re-reads the file itself for the sandbox and for credential variable names. Anything the native loop needs from the global config, such as a tunable compaction threshold that is today the constant COMPACT_AT, has to reach it by one of these two paths.

submit.findings_summary: GlobalConfig (ostra-core/src/config.rs) is a `#[serde(default)]` struct with a hand-written Default and a ts-rs export. It is loaded with `load_toml` from `$OSTRA_CONFIG` or the OS config dir. The server validates only its `[sandbox]` table, through `ostra_sandbox::validate::global`: startup aborts on an issue, and `Shared::global()` re-reads the file per call and falls back to the last good copy. No endpoint writes the global config, and `validate_workspace` takes it as input without validating it. The engine reads `Services::global()` per execution in runner.rs, resolves the route, and folds merged values into `ExecContext` and `ExecutionSpec`. `NativeExecutor` never receives a GlobalConfig. It re-reads config.toml itself in `sandbox_for` and `mcp_secret_vars` with `unwrap_or_default`, which skips the server's last-good fallback. The compaction threshold is the constant `COMPACT_AT = 0.95` in ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs, used in `Run::execute`, with tests and docs/internals/executors.md written around it.
